name: Casino Hold'em
description: Casino Hold'em Poker is a casino table game introduced in 2001 by Stephen Au-Yeung. Based on Texas Hold'em, players compete against the house (not each other). Players make an ante bet, receive two hole cards, see a three-card flop, then decide to fold or place a play bet (2x ante). Best 5-card poker hand wins.

history.origins: Casino Hold'em Poker was introduced by Stephen Au-Yeung in 2001. It was developed to capitalize on the enormous popularity of Texas Hold'em poker by creating a house-banked casino version.
timeline: 2000: Texas Hold'em experiences massive popularity boom
Current: Popular in land-based and online casinos
history.cultural: Popular in casinos globally due to Texas Hold'em's familiarity. The simple two-decision structure (fold or play 2x) makes it accessible to casual players.
history.evolution: The game was designed to offer Texas Hold'em-style play against the house. Unlike poker, there's no bluffing - it's a game of pure chance with house edge. A bonus bet on the player's hole cards plus flop was added as a side bet.

setup.players: Any number of players, each playing individually against the house/dealer. No player vs player action.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack. Standard poker hand rankings apply.
setup.dealing: Each player and dealer receive 2 hole cards face down. 5 community cards dealt in stages: 3-card flop (face up), turn, river.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, casino chips, table with betting areas

rules.objective: Make a better 5-card poker hand than the dealer using your 2 hole cards and 5 community cards.
rules.gameplay: Place ante bet (optional AA bonus side bet). Dealer gives 2 hole cards to each player and themselves. 3-card flop dealt face up. Decision: Fold (lose ante) OR Place play bet (2x ante amount). Turn and river dealt. Dealer reveals hole cards. Best 5-card hand from 7 cards wins. Dealer qualifies with pair of 4s or better.
keyRules: 2 hole cards dealt to player and dealer
Turn and river dealt after play bet
Dealer qualifies with pair of 4s or better
Ante pays enhanced odds by hand strength
Play bet pays even money (1:1) if won

strategy.basic: Always play with a pair or better. Fold with poor hands. The AA bonus is a side bet with high house edge - play only for entertainment.
strategy.intermediate: Optimal strategy is complex but generally: Play with any pair, any ace high, any king high with good kickers, and many queen-high hands. Fold weak hands that don't connect with the flop.
strategy.advanced: Fully optimal strategy involves considering all possible outcomes. Rough guideline: Call with about 60% of hands. The house edge is approximately 2.16% with optimal play. The AA bonus bet has much higher house edge (around 6-7%).
tips: Play any pair after the flop
AA bonus bet is for entertainment only - high house edge
Dealer folds 30% of hands (no pair 4s+) - this is player's advantage
